requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers every obligation, it is marked completely, and the tests cover the main cases. I found no gaps and no FIXME comments. **Implementation** - **Definition badge links to the detail page.** In `replace_definitions` (`src/lib.rs`, marked `{impl}`), the definition badge becomes an `` whenever `DetailPlan::detail_path` (`src/index.rs`, marked `{impl}`) returns a page. Otherwise it stays a ``. The href is built with `chapter_href`, which handles relative links, including `../` from nested chapters. - **"See evidence" link.** The same function appends `

See evidence

` after each rendered requirement or example body. Terms are excluded, which matches the requirement's scope of requirements and examples. - **Detail page links back.** `render_detail_page` (`src/index.rs`, marked `{impl}`) emits `[View definition](chapter_href(detail, definition.path, anchor))`. The anchor comes from `DefinitionKind::anchor`, which is marked `{impl}` and matches the badge `id`. It adds `[Requirements index](…)` only when an index path exists. - **Index rows.** `DetailPlan::populate` (marked `{impl}`) writes the index table rows. Each row links to the detail page through `chapter_href`. - **Reference badges still link to the definition.** `reference_badge` and `replace_inline_references` (both marked `{impl}`) link to the definition's anchored badge. `reference_badge` carries only a `requirements.references.book_badges` marker. The text of `book_badges` itself requires badges that link to the definition, including across nested chapters, so that requirement carries out this part. - **Names containing `.md`.** `chapter_href` ends with `href.replace(".md", "%2Emd")`, with a comment explaining the mdBook behaviour. All the links above go through it, so they resolve for names such as `requirements.cli.mdbook`. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (`src/lib.rs`): - It checks the badge `href` and the "See evidence" link for a requirement, an example, and a `cli.mdbook` requirement, using `%2Emd`-encoded hrefs. - It checks that exactly 3 "See evidence" links appear. - It checks the `[View definition]` back-link, including the `.md` case, and that "Requirements index" is absent when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (`src/index.rs`): - It checks the badge `href`, the index row links, and the `[Requirements index](../../appendix/requirements-index.html) · [View definition]` back-links when an index exists. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (`src/lib.rs`) tests the `.md` encoding in both directions: detail page to definition anchor, and index to detail page. - Reference badges linking to the definition are tested by `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` and the fenced-reference test in `src/lib.rs`. Both are cited under `book_badges`. **Minor observations (not gaps)** - `.md` handling for reference badges is covered only through the shared `chapter_href` unit test. - "See evidence" for a definition nested inside another definition is not tested directly. It goes through the same recursive code path.

text: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
